learning_outcomes.text: Understand the main mechanisms of a computing system.
Address computational problems of limited complexity, providing a foundation for the study of more advanced programming problems and techniques.

Acquire the logical principles of the operation and organization of processing systems and the acquisition of methodologies to exploit their potential, with particular reference to the study and techniques for programming computers.
Understand the functional structure of the main hardware and software modules that make up a processing system.
Understand the techniques and fundamental tools for the use of the computer and for its programming.
Acquire a set of cultural tools to facilitate the study of other topics in their school curriculum and to identify topics for autonomous study.

Acquire the necessary skills for the development of algorithmic solutions for problems of limited complexity and for the coding and development of programs in C language, as a basis for the study of more complex and advanced problems.
Understand the fundamentals of computer science, introducing the principles underlying the operation and organization of computing systems.
Develop the ability to apply knowledge to simple computational problems.
Understand the main concepts related to data representation and storage, data processing, computer networks and the Internet.
Understand the foundations for algorithms and programming languages.
Develop students' ability to translate simple problems into programs (Python programming).

Cover variables and data types, conditionals and loops, strings and input handling, functions, scoping and abstraction, structured data types and mutability, higher-order functions, as well as fundamental testing and debugging techniques.
Introduce the concepts of exceptions and assertions for error handling and for verifying program behavior.

Acquire a solid understanding of the fundamental concepts of computer science and be able to understand the main mechanisms of a computing system, describe and analyze simple algorithms, and develop basic programs in Python.

assessment_rules: The overall examination grade is the average of the grades obtained in the assessments for the two modules (Module A and Module B). For Module A, a minimum score of 18 points is required to pass. For Module B, the overall result is the weighted average of the programming theory test (1/3 weight) and the practical test (2/3 weight). The examination is passed upon obtaining a passing grade (18) in both assessments. An assessment remains valid for two calendar years from the date it was passed; if a student retakes an assessment, the previously obtained result is forfeited, even if passing.
